chunks: And from him, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from one who narrated to him, from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn, from Wahb ibn Hafsh, from Abu Basir, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:

Indeed, the Upriser (Al-Qa'im), peace be upon him, when he rises, will restore the Sacred House (Kaaba) to its foundation, and will restore the Mosque of the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) to its foundation, and will restore the Mosque of Kufa to its foundation.
And Abu Basir said: [The foundation of the Mosque of Kufa was] the place of the Tammarites.

key_terms.التَّمَّارِينَ: The Tammarites (a tribe associated with Kufa)
key_terms.الْقَائِمُ: The Upriser (a title for the Mahdi)
key_terms.مَسْجِدَ رَسُولِ اللَّهِ: The Mosque of the Messenger of Allah

ai.seo_question: What does the Mahdi do to the holy mosques upon his rise?
ai.summary: This narration from Shaykh al-Tusi’s *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* highlights the Mahdi’s role in purifying the sanctuaries by restoring them to their original foundations, a process often interpreted by Shia scholars as rectifying historical alterations and political encroachments. The specific mention of the 'place of the Tammarin' in the Mosque of Kufa underscores the restoration of local Shi'a identity and authority in Iraq, linking the global spiritual renewal of Mecca and Medina with regional religious autonomy.
